newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends stronger on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends stronger on profit-taking.

text.p: The Canadian dollar ended stronger on Tuesday at C$1.3739 (US$0.7276) from Monday's close of C$1.3778 (US$0.7257) on profit-taking against long U.S. dollar positions, traders said.
They said the currency also benefited from steady Canadian dollar buying interest on the crosses against the German mark, which is expected to continue overnight.

"There was a good solid round of profit-taking on long U.S. dollar positions and a fairly healthy round of buying of Canada and selling of marks," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC-Wood Gundy Inc.
Farrill said significant overseas interest in the Canadian dollar outbid domestic pessimism and is setting up the currency for a move to levels as strong as C$1.3715 (US$0.7291).
"Domestically there was a lot of negativity early in the day but I think what we found out today is that internationally, the non-Canadian players aren't nearly as negative to Canada," he said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 82.40 Japanese yen from 81.86 yen at Monday's close. The dollar rallied to 1.2816 German marks from 1.2717 marks on Monday.
